title: Morning Headlines
intro: A Russian missile inside NATO territory, a landmark Gaza disarmament deal, and a record-pace Ebola emergency headline a day of acute global crises.

items.title: Russian Missile Crashes Inside Poland, Triggering NATO Alert
items.subtitle: CNN / Euronews / Irish Times
items.summary: A Russian missile fired during a massive barrage on Ukraine — at least 74 missiles and hundreds of Shahed drones that killed 13 Ukrainians — flew roughly 90 km into Polish territory and exploded in a field. NATO scrambled aircraft, Poland's PM said forces were ready to intercept, and EU Commission President von der Leyen called it an 'unacceptable violation' of EU airspace.

items.title: Trump Announces Historic Hamas Disarmament Agreement for Gaza
items.subtitle: CBS News / Axios / Al Jazeera
items.summary: Trump's 'Board of Peace' announced that Hamas has agreed in principle to full disarmament, with a detailed roadmap due within 14 days. Hamas says disarmament is conditional on Israel ceasing strikes and withdrawing from Gaza; Israel remains skeptical, and implementation faces significant obstacles over a seven-to-eight-month timeline.

items.title: DRC Ebola Outbreak Passes 1,500 Deaths — Fastest-Spreading on Record
items.subtitle: WHO Africa / Mercy Corps / ECDC
items.summary: As of July 29, the 2026 Ituri Ebola outbreak has recorded 3,442 confirmed cases and 1,521 deaths across five DRC provinces, making it the third-largest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever. WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May; cross-border spread to Uganda has raised regional alarm.

items.title: U.S. Q2 GDP Growth Slows to 1.5% as Tariffs and Trade Deficit Bite
items.subtitle: NPR / Fortune / Bloomberg
items.summary: The Commerce Department reported annualized second-quarter GDP growth of just 1.5%, down from 2.1% in Q1, as tariffs, a widening trade deficit, and lower government spending weighed on output. Consumer spending rose 3.2% but is being funded partly by savings drawdowns, a pace economists warn is unsustainable.

items.title: Japan Earthquake Kills 35 in Kumamoto; Rescue Efforts Continue
items.subtitle: Al Jazeera / Japan Times / Korea Times
items.summary: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture on July 28, killing at least 35 people, partly collapsing a shopping mall, and cutting power to nearly 35,000 homes. Rescue teams were still searching for survivors on July 31, with expressways, rail lines, and sections of Kumamoto Castle damaged.
